questions.q: What three jobs does an informal letter body do?
questions.a: Share your news, ask about them, close with something forward-looking (invite/plan/write-back). A wrong answer 'just tell them things' produces the flat postcard-body this node exists to fix.

questions.q: Fix this cold line for a letter to a friend: 'I am writing to inform you of my selection in the school team.'
questions.a: 'You will not believe it — I made the school team!' A wrong answer that only drops 'inform' keeps the reporting stance — the fix is excitement, not vocabulary.

questions.q: Which close earns the warmth mark: 'Yours faithfully' / 'Write back soon, your friend Amit' / 'The end'?
questions.a: The middle — forward-looking and personal. 'Faithfully' is for strangers; 'The end' isn't a letter close at all.

questions.q: An informal letter to a friend or relative keeps the light skeleton — address, date, Dear ___, warm body, loving sign-off — and the body must DO something: share news, ask questions back, invite, thank, or ______.

Fill in the blank: An informal letter to a friend or relative keeps the light skeleton — address, date, Dear ___, warm body, loving sign-off — and the body must DO ______: share news, ask questions back, invite, thank, or apologize.
Fill in the blank: To share (news + reactions), to ask (______ to them), to invite (details + enthusiasm).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student writes a complete informal letter with all blocks and a body that carries a clear purpose (news + questions + a forward-looking close), sustaining warm register throughout.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: To share (news + reactions), to ask (questions to them), to invite (details + ______).
